idiom_name: abstract class with a final template method + protected abstract primitives and protected hooks
implementation_notes: Java methods are virtual by default, so the non-overridable half is written explicitly: declare the public operation `final`, make required steps `protected abstract` and optional steps `protected` methods with a default (often empty) body. The JDK is full of this shape - AbstractList implements most of List on top of the required get(int)/size(), InputStream implements the array reads on top of the required read(), and HttpServlet.service dispatches to the doGet/doPost the application supplies. The classic abstract-class form is still justified whenever the skeleton must hold against subclasses or needs instance state; where no shared state exists, a default method on an interface carries the same skeleton (see the interface-default-method variant).
pitfalls: Drop the `final` modifier and the wrapper is virtual again: any subclass - or a mocking framework - can replace the whole algorithm, which is the hole the pattern closes.

Java hides the difference between required and optional steps in the signature: a subclass that skips a protected abstract member does not compile, but one that skips a hook silently inherits the default, so document which is which.
A protected hook can be widened to public on override, re-exposing the extension point to clients, and calling a hook from the constructor runs before subclass field initialisers.

variants.name: Interface default method as the skeleton (no state)
variants.implementation_notes: Since Java 8 an interface method may have a body, so the skeleton can live on the interface: Iterable.forEach runs a traversal over the required iterator(), and Iterator.forEachRemaining runs the loop over the required hasNext()/next(). Implementors supply only the primitive operations, and the API author can add further steps with default bodies without breaking existing implementations - the reason the feature exists. It replaces the abstract base class where no instance state or constructor is needed; the skeleton cannot be final, so any implementor may replace it.
variants.idiom_name: default method implemented over required interface methods (Iterable.forEach / Iterator.forEachRemaining shape)
pitfalls: A default method cannot be final: unlike an abstract class, the interface cannot stop an implementor from restating export(), so invariant-bearing skeletons stay on abstract classes.
Interfaces hold no instance state, so steps that need shared fields must pass data through the required methods or be moved into an abstract class.
A class implementing two interfaces that both declare a default export() must override it explicitly to resolve the diamond.
